sources.title: GPT-3.5 Turbo model documentation
sources.evidence: The complete current Markdown identifies model ID gpt-3.5-turbo, default snapshot gpt-3.5-turbo-0125, 16,385-token context and text input/output. It explicitly states that API access ended October 23, 2026. The HTML feature table says function calling is unsupported, conflicting with explicit earlier capability announcements; no explanation for that discrepancy is supplied. Reopened for the October 27 parameter re-audit; it provides neither a total nor an activated-parameter count.

sources.title: Introducing ChatGPT and Whisper APIs
sources.evidence: The launch names gpt-3.5-turbo and explains that the unpinned name follows a recommended model while dated snapshots can be selected. Its current displayed date is an April 24, 2024 editorial update, not the original launch date. It documents text messages and code/natural-language tasks. Reopened for the October 27 parameter re-audit; it provides neither a total nor an activated-parameter count.

sources.title: OpenAI API launch announcement, March 1, 2023
sources.evidence: The dated opening announcement by OpenAI developer-relations staff member Logan Kilpatrick states that the ChatGPT and Whisper APIs are now available and links the original launch article. Used only for first-party release timing; replies from other users are not technical evidence.

sources.title: Function calling and other API updates
sources.evidence: June 13, 2023 announcement explicitly adds trained function calling to gpt-3.5-turbo-0613, describes JSON function arguments, and schedules the generic alias upgrade on June 27. It distinguishes the original 0301 snapshot and the then-separate 16K model.

sources.title: New embedding models and API updates
sources.evidence: January 25, 2024 announcement identifies 0125, a fix for non-English function-call encoding, and migration of the generic gpt-3.5-turbo alias from 0613 to 0125. This supports function calling for the alias target; it does not make 0125 the March 2023 launch checkpoint. Reopened for the October 27 parameter re-audit; it provides neither a total nor an activated-parameter count.

sources.title: OpenAI model deprecations
sources.evidence: The April 22, 2026 legacy-model notice records October 23, 2026 shutdown for 0125 and the gpt-3.5-turbo alias. This is service status rather than a change to the model release date or historical capabilities.

sources.title: GPT-4 Technical Report
sources.evidence: The report compares GPT-3.5 Turbo in factuality and safety figures and distinguishes multiple ChatGPT revisions. The reviewed comparisons disclose no Turbo parameter count, active count, or exact dense-versus-expert architecture. Benchmark reasoning performance does not define a dedicated reasoning mode. Freshly reopened PDF and complete-text review on October 27 confirm that the exact Turbo labels in Figures 7 and 9 are performance comparisons, not parameter specifications.

sources.title: Weak-to-Strong Generalization
sources.evidence: The training study explicitly excludes GPT-2, GPT-3 and GPT-3.5 from its GPT-4-family experimental series. GPT-3.5-level performance labels therefore do not disclose the commercial Turbo model architecture or size. Reopened PDF and searched the full freshly cached text on October 27; footnote 1 explicitly rules out treating the GPT-4 experimental series as GPT-3.5 size evidence.

sources.title: Introducing gpt-oss
sources.evidence: The August 2025 release states these were OpenAI’s first open-weight language models since GPT-2. This corroborates the hosted GPT-3.5 Turbo family was not an open-weight release; gpt-oss counts are not transferred to Turbo.

sources.title: OpenAI Services Agreement
sources.evidence: The current agreement applies to OpenAI APIs, reserves service IP rights and provides limited service access. It supports a descriptive proprietary classification, not a named downloadable-checkpoint license or a claim that these exact 2026 terms applied at the 2023 launch.

sources.title: CODEFUSION original preprint, subsequently withdrawn
sources.evidence: Reopened October 27. Original October 2023 Tables 1 and 6 list the exact gpt-3.5-turbo comparison as 20B in the #P column. This is the original source behind a repeated 20B claim, but the authors subsequently withdrew the claim as unverified conjecture (s12); it is rejected, not adopted as a nominal specification. There is no separate activated-count column.

sources.title: CODEFUSION author withdrawal notice
sources.publisher: Mukul Singh et al., Microsoft, via arXiv
sources.evidence: Reopened October 27. The November 1, 2023 v3 withdrawal notice says the ChatGPT parameter count was inappropriately sourced conjecture from a Forbes article with an omitted citation, and that the authors had no direct knowledge or verification. This explicitly disqualifies the original 20B row as verified parameter evidence.

sources.title: CODEFUSION revised camera-ready paper
sources.evidence: Reopened October 27. Tables 1 and 6 define #P as model parameter count and now mark the exact gpt-3.5-turbo row Unknown. The neighboring text-davinci-003 row has a separate 175B value; that is not a Turbo size or unchanged-lineage disclosure. The revised paper has no separate active-count specification.

sources.title: CODEFUSION final EMNLP 2023 proceedings paper
sources.publisher: Mukul Singh et al., Microsoft / ACL Anthology
sources.evidence: Reopened October 27 and checked Tables 1 and 6, PDF pages 4 and 10. The final proceedings agree with the Microsoft revised copy: gpt-3.5-turbo has Unknown in #P. This confirms the correction persisted into the published original research, rather than relying on the retracted preprint.

sources.title: RAD-Bench: Evaluating Large Language Models’ Capabilities in Retrieval Augmented Dialogues
sources.publisher: Tzu-Lin Kuo et al., MediaTek Research and National Taiwan University / ACL Anthology
sources.evidence: Reopened October 27. The original 2025 study explicitly includes an Activated Params. column in Table 2, PDF page 5, but GPT-3.5-Turbo is marked with a dash; its 16k context is a separate column. Section 4.1 dates closed-model response collection to July 2024. This later research-team comparison supplies no active count for Turbo, and does not pin a snapshot. Its reported active counts for other models are not transferred.

sources.title: DeepSeek-V2: A Strong, Economical, and Efficient Mixture-of-Experts Language Model
sources.evidence: Reopened October 27. Tables 2 and 3 explicitly separate activated and total parameters for their listed open models, but do not include GPT-3.5 Turbo. GPT-3.5-Turbo-0613 appears in Table 5 and GPT-3.5-Turbo in Table 9 only as performance comparisons. These exact labels therefore supply neither a total nor an active parameter count.

family.note: Use the specific GPT-3.5 family rather than generic GPT.

parameters_b.note: Fresh October 27 review found no supported total for the gpt-3.5-turbo alias or its 0125 target in current OpenAI Docs, launch/update material or OpenAI research. The original CODEFUSION 20B row was explicitly withdrawn as unverified secondary conjecture; both the Microsoft revised copy and final proceedings replace it with Unknown. GPT-3’s 175B total is not transferable without an explicit unchanged named lineage.

active_parameters_b.note: Independently rechecked active counts on October 27, including later original research tables. RAD-Bench Table 2 has an explicit Activated Params. column but marks GPT-3.5-Turbo with a dash. DeepSeek-V2 separates total and activated counts for other models, while its Turbo comparisons give only performance. No supported active-count convention for the exact alias or 0125 target was found; neither a total nor assumed dense architecture supplies one.

architecture.note: Targeted first-party architecture, training and interpretability searches did not verify a dense or expert-routed design for this exact alias target. Later research comparison labels do not establish production architecture. Keep null.

context_window.note: Exact last-documented context for the alias’s 0125 target, not the original March 2023 snapshot. The service is now shut down; this does not assert current endpoint availability.

modalities.note: The model documentation specifies text input/output; code is text, not a separate modality.

reasoning.note: Clear the unsupported false assertion. Reviewed sources do not explicitly define support or non-support for a dedicated reasoning mode; general reasoning benchmarks do not resolve this flag.

tool_call.note: Historical model capability is explicitly documented: 0613 introduced trained function calling, the alias upgraded, and 0125 fixed function-call encoding. The current HTML feature table conflicts by saying unsupported; retain the explicit release evidence and record the conflict rather than erase historical support. This is not a claim that the shut-down API works today or that 0301 had the feature.

patch.notes: The alias launched March 1, 2023 and last pointed to gpt-3.5-turbo-0125; its 16,385-token context describes that later target, not the original 0301 snapshot. Function calling is documented by the June 2023 upgrade and January 2024 release, despite a conflicting current model-page feature table. OpenAI shut down API access on October 23, 2026. Total and active parameter counts remain undisclosed. The CODEFUSION 20B claim was withdrawn; its revised tables say Unknown, and RAD-Bench leaves the active count blank. Exact architecture remains unverified.

summary: Fresh parameter re-audit retains explicit null total and active counts. Reopened OpenAI documentation and research; rejected the withdrawn CODEFUSION 20B conjecture against the author notice and corrected final tables, and checked later RAD-Bench and DeepSeek-V2 active-count comparisons. Preserved the other twelve assessments, including original alias release, later 0125 context, historical function calling and the recorded current-table conflict and shutdown.
